reason: Re-derived from the VPC user guide page How Amazon VPC works, section Access a corporate or home network; the VPN user guide says the same.
answer: A Site-to-Site VPN connection consists of two (2) VPN tunnels between a virtual private gateway or transit gateway on the AWS side and a customer gateway device in your data center.
quote: A Site-to-Site VPN connection consists of two VPN tunnels between a virtual private gateway or transit gateway on the AWS side, and a customer gateway device located in your data center.

reason: Re-derived from the AWS Organizations FAQ, question What is a resource control policy (RCP)?
answer: An RCP is an AWS Organizations policy with preventative controls on AWS resources: it centrally sets the maximum available permissions to your AWS resources. Typical use: restrict access to your resources so that only identities that belong to your organization can access them, or set the conditions under which identities external to your organization can access them.
quote: Using RCPs, you can centrally set the maximum available permissions to your AWS resources as you scale your workloads on AWS. For example, an RCP can help restrict access to your resources so that they can only be accessed by identities that belong to your organization, or specifying the conditions under which identities external to your organization can access your resources.

answer: A role trust policy is a required resource-based policy attached to an IAM role; its Principal element defines the principals that you trust to assume the role (who can assume the role), for example accounts, users, roles or services.

reason: Re-derived from the AWS Architecture Blog post Overview of Data Transfer Costs for Common Architectures, section Accessing services within the same AWS Region.
answer: Yes. Through an internet gateway to the public endpoint of a service in the same Region there are no data transfer charges; through a NAT gateway there is a data processing charge per gigabyte (GB) for data that passes through the gateway.
quote: If the internet gateway is used to access the public endpoint of the AWS services in the same Region (Figure 1 – Pattern 1), there are no data transfer charges. If a NAT gateway is used to access the same services (Figure 1 – Pattern 2), there is a data processing charge (per gigabyte (GB)) for data that passes through the gateway.

answer: There are two (2) types. Customer-managed prefix lists are sets of IP address ranges that you define and manage, and you can share them with other AWS accounts. AWS-managed prefix lists are sets of IP address ranges for AWS services; you cannot create, modify, share, or delete an AWS-managed prefix list.
quote: Sets of IP address ranges for AWS services. You cannot create, modify, share, or delete an AWS-managed prefix list.

reason: Re-derived from the AWS Certification Before Testing policy page, section Beta exams; the Certification FAQ What is a beta exam? gives the same purpose.
answer: A beta exam validates the performance of exam questions before they are used on standard versions of the exam. It differs from the standard exam: it contains more total questions and more scored questions, is available for a limited period (generally 1 to 3 months), and is offered at a discount. Passing it still earns the certification.
quote: A beta exam contains more total questions and more scored questions than the standard version of the same exam.

reason: Re-derived from the VPC user guide page NAT gateway basics.
answer: If the NAT gateway's Availability Zone is down, resources in the other Availability Zones lose internet access. AWS advises one NAT gateway per Availability Zone with routing that keeps resources on the NAT gateway in their own zone.
quote: If you have resources in multiple Availability Zones and they share one NAT gateway, and if the NAT gateway's Availability Zone is down, resources in the other Availability Zones lose internet access.

reason: Re-derived from the AWS Organizations user guide page Resource control policies (RCPs), section RCP effects on permissions and the SCP/RCP note at the top.
answer: An RCP affects every principal that tries to access a resource in a member account with an applicable RCP, whether or not the principal belongs to the same organization, including root users; service-linked roles are the exception. Choose an RCP over an SCP when you need to restrict IAM principals that are external to your organization from accessing resources in your member accounts (an SCP limits principals inside your member accounts).
quote: RCPs impact the effective permissions of principals trying to access resources in a member account with an applicable RCP, regardless of whether the principals belong to the same organizations or not. This includes root users.

reason: Re-derived from the IAM user guide page Generate credential reports for your AWS account.
answer: The report includes only passwords, the first two (2) access keys per user, MFA devices and X.509 signing certificates. It leaves out service-specific credentials (for example CodeCommit passwords, Amazon Bedrock or CloudWatch Logs long-term API keys) and any user access keys beyond the first two.
quote: The IAM credential report only includes the following IAM-managed credentials: passwords, the first two access keys per user, MFA devices, and X.509 signing certificates.

reason: Re-derived from the Amazon VPC pricing page, NAT gateway pricing example; the Network Firewall pricing page says the same.
answer: Only when the instance and the NAT gateway are in different Availability Zones; in the same Availability Zone the traffic uses private IP addresses and has no data transfer charge.
quote: There will be data transfer charges between your NAT gateway and EC2 instance if they are in a different Availability Zone.

reason: Re-derived from the VPC user guide page Enable VPC internet access using internet gateways, section Internet gateway basics.
answer: The internet gateway logically provides one-to-one (1:1) NAT for the instance: outbound traffic gets the instance's public IPv4 or Elastic IP address as its reply address instead of the private address, and inbound traffic to that public or Elastic IP address is translated to the instance's private IPv4 address. The instance only knows its private address.
quote: The internet gateway logically provides the one-to-one NAT on behalf of your instance, so that when traffic leaves your VPC subnet and goes to the internet, the reply address field is set to the public IPv4 address or Elastic IP address of your instance, and not its private IP address.

reason: Re-derived from the VPC user guide page on Elastic IP addresses; the EC2 user guide adds that an Elastic IP address is for use in a specific Region only and cannot be moved to a different Region.
answer: Regional. Elastic IP addresses are regional: an Elastic IP address is for use in a specific Region only and cannot be moved to another Region (use Global Accelerator for global static IP addresses).
quote: Elastic IP addresses are regional.
